set.body:
Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-later; milestone-maintenance.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: Acceptance retained; this audit did not run its proposed tests.

Remaining / next action: ADR-first proposal for normalized Segmentation/SegmentLink/Coded on-disk input, only when a concrete second consumer requires it. Reuse current prepare/exchange contracts; if prepare actually needs this format, record the prerequisite promotion before coding.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

Scheduling lane: later. Governing plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19: Canonical corpus interchange is distinct from mapping output. Park the ADR-first proposal until a concrete second consumer needs it; do not gate shared mapping evidence or preview on a universal intake format.

Historical finding and scope retained below; current acceptance ownership above governs.

The intake pipeline normalizes INTO MEMORY AND STOPS. Verified 2026-09-17: there is no Encoder/Decoder for Segmentation, SegmentLink or Coded anywhere in corpus or corpus-intake; circe is used only to read legacy manifests and descriptors. Consequences:
- every consumer re-reads raw files with its own logic (the Python scorers read Sherlock-shaped TSVs);
- every new corpus needs a hand-written intake object (FriendsIntake, MementoIntake);
- the only wild-format reader is Xlsx.scala, and SherlockAnnotations parses TSV on a separate, unreconciled path.

Proposal: a declared, versioned on-disk form of the normalized model, read by every consumer instead of raw files, which turns per-corpus intake objects into data (a profile plus a descriptor). This was the owner's question on 2026-09-17: whether there is a preferred format that idiosyncratic ones convert into.

Constraints: the emission carries descriptions, so under rule 14(d) it lives under the git-ignored data root, never in the repository. Content identity already exists for CorpusProfile and, since ecc0bc2f, for Segmentation; an emission should carry it. This is new vocabulary, so the ADR comes FIRST (SD5): this bead is the ADR and children follow it.

Related, not duplicated: bd-01M2TABFW72D8WWQF481SD37KW (ADR 0007 amendment, canonical form for D1A types, docs only) and the recall-map output schema (bd-01M2TADC4VKSDZ2S9SXETH2MYM).
